column1: # class-overrides.tsv — per-class accommodations for run-netty-suite.sh
# THIS FILE IS TRACKED IN GIT ON PURPOSE. `apps/` is gitignored wholesale
# (.gitignore:12), so every file in this fixture has to be force-added
# (`git add -f`) to exist in the repo at all — this script's own header claimed
# the table was "tracked in git" while the whole netty runner was untracked.
# WHAT THIS IS FOR
# The flat --timeout cap (default 180s) is a single number for ~730 classes of
# wildly different weight. A class that legitimately needs longer than the cap
# is killed and recorded HANG — indistinguishable in the results from a real
# deadlock, and expensive to re-triage every round. An entry here raises the cap
# for one class (never lowers it: the effective timeout is max(default, entry))
# and/or adds VM flags for it.
# FORMAT: tab-separated  <class>  <timeout_seconds>  <extra_flags>
# Use `-` for a column that does not apply. Blank lines and '#' lines ignored.
# Print the loaded table with:  run-netty-suite.sh overrides
# DnsNameResolverTest drives 232 tests through a live in-process DNS server and
# is simply a long class: 118s on an idle host, 125s inside a 6-shard run, and
# 147s (82% of the 180s cap) with five CPU burners alongside — all three runs
# byte-identical at ok=216 aborted=16. A saturated full-suite run has no headroom
# left, and a class killed at the cap is reported HANG, which is exactly how this
# class was first characterized. 600s is generous rather than marginal on purpose.
# See docs/internal/fixed-suite-bugs/netty/dnsnameresolvertest-windows-only-aborts-CONFIRMED-20260819.md
io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsNameResolverTest
